sn48.18:1.6: While it the five qualities of faith, etc., are found among those who are unenlightened, and even, as potential, among all beings, it is only on entering the noble path that they are considered “faculties” with the decisive power to overcome their opposites. | The expression “stands outside in the faction of ordinary persons” is found only here and [sn55.40:2.1](). In both cases it indicates individuals who are not noble ones, but who nonetheless may be Buddhists. _Bāhira_ (“outside”) here should be distinguished from the more common _bāhiraka_ (“outsider”), which refers to non-Buddhists.
